current_activity: Bluecoat: advances from the Caumont ridge at about 07:00 with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade towards Point 309
notes: Event date: 30 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 388, 390, 391). Event definition: The division, with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade in support and the 11th Armoured Division on its right, begins its advance a few minutes before 07:00 from the Caumont ridge; the first objectives (two villages near Caumont, then les Loges and Point 226) are taken by about 10:00 and Point 309 is the objective of the day; mines put seven Churchills and two flail tanks out of action (pp. 388 and 390). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 388: "Point 309. It is marked by a quarry show- ing just below the summit and was the first day's objective of VIII Corps' 15th Division"; pp. 390-391: "with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade in support, and the 11th Armoured Division on their right began their advance a few minutes before seven". Location approximate: the point is Caumont, from which the advance started; Point 309 itself is not located. Location support: Ellis names the Caumont ridge as the start and Point 309 as the objective, which is not in the gazetteers used (pp. 388 and 390). current_activity: Crosses the Seine in stormboats and Dukws near St. Pierre-du-Vauvray; the bridgeheads join by 11:00 on 28 August
notes: Event date: 27 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 455, 467). Event definition: The division assaults across the Seine on 27 August: one brigade crosses in stormboats, followed by Dukws, near St. Pierre-du-Vauvray, about two miles from Louviers, losing three boats and suffering heavy casualties, and a second crosses near Portejoie; by 11:00 on 28 August the two bridgeheads are joined and the third brigade crosses at Muids (p. 467). current_activity: Veritable: the 46th Brigade clears Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captures Kranenburg
notes: Event date: 8 February 1945 (by dark) (Ellis, vol. II, p. 259). Event definition: On 8 February the division is to seize the key ground about Cleve after breaching the Siegfried defences; it leads with two brigades, the 46th on the right and the 227th on the left, who have more trouble with mines and mud than with the enemy; with close support from artillery and flame-throwers the 46th Brigade clears the long straggling village of Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captures Kranenburg; the 44th Brigade, which is to force the Siegfried line, is delayed on a rough track and begins only at four in the morning (p. 259). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 259: "The 15th Divisional Group was faced with the task of seizing the key ground about Cleve, first breaching the Siegfried defences on the way"; "the 46th Brigade had cleared the long straggling village of Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captured Kranenburg". Location: Kranenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Kranenburg; the division headquarters is not named and Frasselt, also cleared, lies a few kilometres to the south-east. Location support: Ellis names Kranenburg as the village the 227th Brigade captured (p. 259). current_activity: Veritable: the 44th Brigade breaches the Siegfried defences and reaches the Bresserberg ridge by dark, by Cleve
notes: Event date: 9 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 262). Event definition: On 9 February the day's most important advances are made by the 44th Brigade, supported by tanks of the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade and equipments of the 79th Armoured Division: it begins before dawn against the Siegfried defences just north-east of Frasselt, has three crossings of the anti-tank ditch in use by nine o'clock, collects some 200 prisoners from adjacent trenches and, within another hour, another 200, enters Nutterden, and as darkness falls gains a sound footing on the Bresserberg ridge, just off the western outskirts of Cleve and barely a mile from Materborn village; troops of the German 7th Parachute Division fail to regain the ridge in the evening, but the road between Cleve and Materborn is still blocked (p. 262). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 262: "The day's most important advances were made by the 44th Brigade"; "The advance had begun before dawn against the Siegfried defences just north-east of Frasselt"; "gained a sound footing on the Bresserberg ridge, just off the western outskirts of Cleve and barely a mile from Materborn village". Location: Cleve, North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0578), the town beside the Bresserberg ridge with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Cleve, about two kilometres east of the Bresserberg ridge; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis puts the Bresserberg ridge just off the western outskirts of Cleve (p. 262). current_activity: Veritable: fights its way into Cleve against determined opposition; the town is cleared and handed over next day
notes: Event date: 11 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 264). Event definition: On 11 February the division fights its way into Cleve against determined opposition and enables the 43rd Division's brigade to disengage, though not before that brigade has broken up an early morning attack by paratroops and taken 180 of them prisoner; hardly a house is standing in Cleve and next day the town is finally cleared and handed over to the 3rd Canadian Division; the 46th Brigade then sets out for Calcar with a mobile column (p. 264). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 264: "On the 11th the 15th Division had fought their way into Cleve against determined opposition"; "next day the town was finally cleared and handed over to the 3rd Canadian Division". current_activity: Veritable: takes over the attack at the escarpment; forces the inner anti-tank ditch; fighting in Goch by midnight
notes: Event date: 18 February 1945, to midnight (Ellis, vol. II, p. 267). Event definition: After the 43rd Division has secured the escarpment north-east of Goch on the 17th and its engineers have opened seven crossings over the outer anti-tank ditch, the 15th Division's leading brigade takes up the attack on the morning of 18 February; greatly helped by the special equipments of the 79th Armoured Division the Scots force an inner anti-tank ditch and by midnight are fighting in the environs of Goch, as are troops of the 53rd Division to their right and a brigade of the 51st on the far side of the Niers; the garrison commander surrenders the next day, but confused fighting in the rubble goes on for another 48 hours (p. 267). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. current_activity: Plunder: assaults the Rhine opposite Xanten at 02:00 with two brigades; stone-pitched bank splits the left attack
notes: Event date: 24 March 1945, 02:00 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 289, 290, 291). Event definition: At 02:00 on 24 March the XII Corps assault by the 15th (Scottish) Division opposite Xanten begins, with two brigades and four battalions mounted in Buffaloes and stormboats; on the right the two-battalion attack goes according to the book and its immediate objectives are secured before first light; on the left, against the German 7th Parachute Division, a mile and a half of stone-pitched far bank stops the Buffaloes, the battalion assaults are widely separated and immediate objectives are still being fought for at first light; early in the afternoon the right-hand brigade joins the 6th Airborne Division (pp. 289-290). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 289: "At 2 a.m. on the 24th the United States Ninth Army's assault south of Wesel and the XII Corps assault by the 15th (Scottish) Division opposite Xanten began"; "The assault in the Xanten sector by two brigades of 15th Division was made by four battalions mounted in Buffaloes and stormboats"; "On the right the two-battalion attack went according to the book, immediate objectives being secured before first light"; pp. 290-291: "the right-hand brigade of the 15th Division found the German defence on their front so loosened up that they joined forces early in the afternoon with the 6th Airborne Division". Location: Xanten, North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0697) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Xanten; the division crossed the Rhine opposite it and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Xanten as the sector the division assaulted opposite (p. 289). current_activity: Advance to the Elbe: leads VIII Corps on the Celle-Uelzen axis; reaches Celle against patchy opposition on the 12th
notes: Event date: 12 April 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 309). Event definition: On 11 April VIII Corps advances on the Celle-Uelzen axis with the 15th Division and, on minor roads to the left, the 11th Armoured Division; the 15th Division reaches Celle against patchy opposition on the 12th and has to bridge the Aller before it can go on; demolitions on the main road hold it back next day, but it switches to a minor road and makes a fast advance that night (p. 309). current_activity: Uelzen: has closed in on the town from the 15th and attacks it; Uelzen is captured on 18 April
notes: Event date: 18 April 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 309, 310, 311). Event definition: After the 15th Division is almost into Uelzen just before daylight on 14 April, meets a German group from the 233rd Panzer Training Division and the improvised Panzer Division Clausewitz and beats off a night counter-attack after bitter hand-to-hand fighting, it closes in on the town on the 15th and attacks it while the 6th Airborne and 11th Armoured Divisions by-pass it; a regimental group of the Clausewitz Division escapes on the night of the 17th and Uelzen is captured next day, 18 April (the page does not name the capturing unit) (pp. 309-311). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 309: "On the 15th the division closed in on the town"; pp. 310-311: "While the 15th Division attacked the town"; "next day Uelzen was captured". current_activity: Elbe: one brigade and a Commando brigade assault across the Elbe below Lauenburg at 02:00; first bridge that night
notes: Event date: 29 April 1945, 02:00 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 337). Event definition: At 02:00 on 29 April, on completion of a strong artillery bombardment, one brigade of the 15th (Scottish) Division and a Commando brigade assault across the Elbe below Lauenburg in Buffaloes and stormboats supported by DD tanks; two brigades follow up, rafts are built, ferries established and the first bridge is opened that night; opposition is not great and over 1,350 prisoners are taken that day (p. 337). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 337: "Twenty-First Army Group's VIII Corps had crossed the Elbe below Lauenburg"; "At two o'clock that morning, on completion of strong artillery bombardment, one brigade of the 15th (Scottish) Division and a Commando brigade assaulted across the river in Buffaloes and stormboats supported by D.D. tanks". Location: Lauenburg/Elbe, Schleswig-Holstein (existing place PL0658) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Lauenburg; the crossing was below it on the Elbe and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the crossing as below Lauenburg (p. 337).
